finding.title: Split epic_18_track_overhaul_test.dart and epic_19_offline_first_test.dart under the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: Files past 400 lines exceed per-file agent read budgets and become dumping grounds for unrelated stories, per AG-3's own stated rationale. This is systemic to the 'one file per epic' convention documented in learning_tracker/CLAUDE.md, which has no split policy even though the repo already practices ad hoc splitting elsewhere (epic_18_story_18x_track_restore_test.dart exists precisely as an epic_18 overflow file, and other epics run past 3000 lines).
finding.recommendation: Formalize the overflow-file pattern already used for epic_18 (split by story range with an _storyNNx_ suffix) as the documented convention in learning_tracker/CLAUDE.md, or add a story_acceptance-specific exemption to AG-3 the way AG-5 already exempts this directory from mirroring.
acceptance_criteria: find learning_tracker/test -name '*_test.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400' either excludes these two files after a split, or story_acceptance carries a documented/checked AG-3 exemption

finding.title: Log the empty catch(_) blocks swallowing temp-dir cleanup failures in epic_19_offline_first_test.dart
finding.why: EH-3 bans empty and log-less catches repo-wide. If Directory.delete(recursive: true) fails here — e.g. a held SQLite file handle on the just-closed content/read-only DB — the failure is silently discarded, leaving stray temp dirs with no breadcrumb that cleanup ever failed, exactly the swallowed-exception debugging dead-end EH-3 exists to prevent.
finding.recommendation: At minimum print/log the caught error instead of a bare catch (_) {} in both addTearDown blocks.
acceptance_criteria: grep -n 'catch (_) {}' learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_19_offline_first_test.dart returns no match, or each site logs the caught error

finding.title: Deduplicate seedProfile/seedProfileZero between test/helpers/drift_memory.dart and test/helpers/test_database.dart
finding.why: Two files under test/helpers/ define an identically-named seedProfile(UserDatabase) — and seedProfileZero — with near-identical bodies (same fixture email, tier, displayName). Three of my four batch files import it interchangeably from either helper. If either copy is fixed or extended (e.g. a new required column) without the other, tests silently diverge on what 'a seeded profile' means depending on which import a test author happened to copy — the same 'divergent parallel copies' failure AG-4 targets for lib/, reproduced in test/helpers/.
finding.recommendation: Keep one implementation (drift_memory.dart looks like the more focused, Drift-specific home) and have test_database.dart re-export or delegate to it; repoint all story_acceptance imports at the single source.
acceptance_criteria: Only one definition of seedProfile and one of seedProfileZero exist under learning_tracker/test/helpers/
grep -rn 'Future<void> seedProfile(' learning_tracker/test/helpers/ returns exactly one match per function name
